correctness.rationale: The proof exactly identifies the parity cut B=I+S^{-1}+wS^((n-1)/2), rewrites it over the integer cyclic lattice as T^2+wT+I using n odd, and identifies its cokernel with that of C_w^n-I_2. A monic quadratic gives the rank-two free integral module; gcd of entries and determinant 2-L_n give Smith factors including all singular boundaries. Finite cyclic-character orthogonality proves the complete flat Schmidt spectrum over every Z/dZ, including composite d. Two independent full scripts then check 104 exact integer Smith instances, many direct modular-image counts, and direct small-state eigenvalue spectra; these checks support but do not replace the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: No assessed primary result or accessible matching earlier finding proves the weighted Möbius-ladder all-odd-length, all-integer-weight, all-prime-or-composite-dimension integer Smith and complete Schmidt-spectrum formula. General bipartite graph-state rank techniques and circulant Smith methods are acknowledged; they do not themselves state or evaluate this two-factor arithmetic family. A nearby generalized-Petersen graph-state result is prime-dimensional, uses a different graph and cut, and does not imply the stated classification. Historical uniqueness is not certified; plausible unindexed work and incomplete access to the full text of that neighboring record remain residual risks.
residual_risks: The full primary text of the published generalized-Petersen finding could not be inspected; only its substantive public abstract and graph-family relationship were available.

The general theory of integer circulant cokernels might imply the explicit recurrence when specialized; no source evaluating this precise quantum-graph-state family was found, and unindexed prior formulations cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The family is a natural symmetric twisted cubic network with a physically meaningful tunable rung controlled-phase weight. The finding is a complete closed entanglement classification over all odd circumferences, every integer weight and all composite qudit dimensions, not a single numerical instance. A nontrivial integral rank-two reduction explains arithmetic entanglement loss and exposes two qualitatively different resonances: three-periodic torsion at unit weight and size-dependent torsion at weight negative two. This supplies a reusable finite-size entanglement-resource benchmark not determined by general graph-state rank criteria alone.
